plates.title: Judge John Overton
plates.credit: Nell Savage Mahoney Papers, THS VI-C-1, Box 34, Folder 74, image ID 30214. Tennessee Historical Society, Tennessee Virtual Archive. Original painting at Travellers Rest Historic House Museum.
plates.rights: TeVA marks this photographic copy No Copyright – United States.
plates.alt: Monochrome portrait of Judge Overton in a dark coat and white cravat, with two quill pens and books beside him.
plates.caption: The museum identifies the two volumes as the Tennessee Reports. Earl’s 1817 logbook records Overton ordering his own portrait and one of Jackson at the same time.
plates.placement: Use this likeness for the living portrait custodian. The mantel placement is an editorial choice. Match the face, cravat, pose, quills and books to this image.

plates.title: Andrew Jackson
plates.credit: National Portrait Gallery, Smithsonian Institution. Transfer from the National Gallery of Art, gift of the A.W. Mellon Educational and Charitable Trust, 1942. Frame conserved with funds from the Smithsonian Women’s Committee. NPG.65.78.
plates.rights: The Smithsonian marks this digital image CC0.
plates.alt: Oil portrait of Andrew Jackson in a dark military uniform with gold epaulettes, a distant landscape visible behind him.
plates.caption: Earl painted both men. The National Portrait Gallery dates this military portrait tentatively to 1817. The identity of the Jackson canvas commissioned by Overton remains unverified.
plates.placement: Introduce Jackson as Overton’s friend and correspondent. Label this the Smithsonian comparison portrait. Use the archive’s original color profile as the visual reference.

plates.title: From Overton to Jackson
plates.credit: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, Andrew Jackson Papers. Item maj012882, first image.
plates.rights: The Library of Congress designates its digital scans of the Andrew Jackson Papers as public domain.
plates.alt: A handwritten letter in dark cursive on pale paper, with a date line and closely spaced lines of writing.
plates.caption: The first sheet of Overton’s letter lets visitors inspect the handwriting of Jackson’s correspondent. It dates from Jackson’s first presidential term.
plates.placement: Place the first sheet on the writing desk with a magnifier. Link the complete archival sequence. Use the 1828 invitation for the earlier election.

plates.title: An invitation on satin
plates.credit: Library of Congress, Rare Book and Special Collections Division, Printed Ephemera Collection, Portfolio 174, Folder 20.
plates.rights: 1828 U.S. imprint. The collection’s rights note identifies exceptions on individual records. This record carries no item-specific restriction.
plates.alt: An eagle and ornamental arch frame a small block of type printed on a folded piece of satin with frayed edges.
plates.caption: Nashville organizers invited guests to Mr. Edmondson’s hotel for December 23 to mark Jackson’s election. The document records what they planned.
plates.placement: Lay this invitation flat in the campaign drawer. Preserve the textile edge and fold. Its printed date and proposed event date are distinct.

plates.title: A leaf from the Tennessee Reports
plates.date: Decision of November 1791 · digitized printed edition
plates.maker: Tennessee Superior Court of Law and Equity
plates.credit: Harvard Law School Library, Caselaw Access Project. Murfree v. Leeper, 1 Tenn. 1 (1 Overt. 1).
plates.rights: Harvard releases its Caselaw Data and metadata under CC0. The held file is the CAP case PDF.
plates.alt: A printed law-report page headed Tennessee Reports and Mero District, with the case name Murfree v. Leeper above the text.
plates.caption: The case begins on page one of volume one. The parallel citation, 1 Overt. 1, ties it to Overton as reporter. The case predates his judgeship.
plates.placement: Use this scan as an inspectable leaf. The original PDF holds both pages. Edition and binding of Overton’s personal copy are unverified.

plates.title: Tennessee before statehood
plates.credit: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division. G3960 1795 .R4 TIL, digital ID g3960.ct007136.
plates.rights: The division identifies its digitized maps as free to use and reuse absent an item advisory. This record lists none.
plates.alt: An engraved map on a creased sheet shows rivers and a long outlined territory extending westward, with a title block at the lower right.
plates.caption: This copy presents the territory to a late-eighteenth-century map reader. Its markings reflect the mapmaker’s perspective.
plates.placement: Open on the entry map table. Keep the printed title and margins visible, allow enlargement, and label it as a regional map. Interpret the earlier Native settlement from the site-specific archaeological record.

plates.title: The center hall, facing north
plates.credit: Historic American Buildings Survey, HABS TN-14, photograph 6. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
plates.rights: HABS reports no known restrictions on U.S. government images. This is a HABS field photograph by Boucher.
plates.alt: View down the entry hall with the stair rising at left, a chair rail, a door ahead and a tall clock farther back.
plates.caption: The view from inside the south entrance shows the stair on the left, the dado height and the door ahead. Use it with the first-floor plan.
plates.placement: Match the visitor’s camera at the entrance and align stair, door, wall trim and floorboards. Date furniture and paint decisions separately.

plates.title: The house in autumn light
plates.credit: Photographs in Carol M. Highsmith’s America Project in the Carol M. Highsmith Archive, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. LC-DIG-highsm-68574.
plates.rights: The item carries the advisory “No known restrictions on publication.”
plates.alt: A daylight photograph of the two-story clapboard house, with green shutters, a red door, autumn leaves and deep tree shadows.
plates.caption: This dated color view shows painted wood and dappled light on the façade. Its visible doorway differs from the projecting portico in the 1970 survey photograph.
plates.placement: Use for observed modern color relationships and lighting. Retain the chosen survey geometry. Calibrate materials separately from shadows in the photograph.

plates.title: The measured south front
plates.credit: Historic American Buildings Survey, HABS TN-14, printed page 9, south elevation. Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
plates.rights: The HABS advisory distinguishes federal field images from copied material. The sheet credits Patrick W. Crawford’s tracing of an architectural firm’s drawing. Use the held PDF for model study and link the federal copy for visitors.
plates.alt: Survey elevation of the south façade with five bays, two end chimneys, a central portico and a scale bar.
plates.caption: The survey elevation records the restored façade. Bay spacing and the position of the portico can be tested against the photograph of the south front.
plates.placement: Builder reference in the source PDF. Use the scale on printed page 9 to set bay spacing and align to the site plan.

references.title: Mary McConnell White May Overton
references.caption: The museum catalogs a portrait of Mary, who married Judge Overton in 1820. Identify her by her full name to distinguish her from later relatives with similar names.
references.use: Link to the museum record. Its catalog page does not establish reuse terms for the digital image.

references.title: William and Franklin
references.caption: The museum identifies William, age twelve, and Franklin, age seven, as brothers whom Judge Overton purchased on October 3, 1832. The records point to the Claybrooke Collection at the state archives.
references.use: Use both named records and a present-day editorial caption. The museum and state archives are listed as rights holders for the scans. Keep the document images at their source pending reuse terms.

references.title: A ceramic bowl from the site
references.caption: The museum identifies a ceramic vessel with a notched rim and burned freshwater snail shells. Its collection also documents a clay hearth and excavated clay effigy.
references.use: Link to the museum object photograph and give visitors the site context. Its image rights and metric dimensions have not been established for a replica.
